::: {.why}
Options are the only instrument this year where the two sides have completely different risk, and getting that asymmetry into your hands now makes phase 8 a mathematics problem rather than a vocabulary problem.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Draw the four basic payoff diagrams at expiry from memory, with the axes labelled and the break-even marked.
- Say what the seller of a put is obliged to do, when, and what their worst case is in dollars.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>55 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Watch the options lecture from MIT 15.401 as far as payoff diagrams and put-call parity. Stop before any pricing model. Pricing is week 36 and you will do it properly there.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} From the saved AAPL chain, pick the nearest expiry and build the payoff at expiry of a bought call, a sold call, a bought put and a sold put at the closest-to-spot strike, using the mid of bid and ask as the premium. Plot all four on one figure and mark the break-evens.
:::
